classification_reasons: Blast radius: the change's core artifact, plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py, is registered on every Bash/PowerShell tool call in every phase, in CI and by hand (plugin/hooks/hooks.json), and plugin/ci/settings.ci.json/run_phase.py rewrite a sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite list every CI phase job reads -- not a few-file, low-risk surface, even though this round's own diff is five lint-only files.
Risk list: sdlc.yaml: risk_list item 'auth' is touched end to end and owner-accepted (status.yaml: risk_accepted: [auth]), not closed by a tight no-concern spec.
Tests: the ~1000-line tokenizer/resolver in shell_guard.py is new code with its own dedicated, large test suite; it is not code the pre-existing suite already covered before this change.
attempted: Intent: this round is the fix for the lint-only review comment (#5488970969, 2026-10-12T09:40:20Z) on PR #152; it does not touch intent.md's problem at all. Confirmed in fix-requests.json that the comment asked for exactly two mechanical actions and nothing else, and the diff matches both: (1) pyproject.toml[tool.ruff.lint.isort].known-first-party gains "lessons", (2) ruff format tests/test_hooks.py. No scope creep beyond the comment.

Spec and plan: no change to spec.md (owner's own instruction, 'choice 164'), none made. plan.md's 'Files that change' now lists pyproject.toml, plugin/gate/checks.py, tests/test_gate.py, tests/test_lessons.py (new bullets) and tests/test_hooks.py (already listed, satisfying the owner's 'one path per bullet' ask); plugin/gate/checks.py was moved out of the 'Not touched' paragraph as required. Verified these five files are exactly the set the diff's own --stat-equivalent section changes for this round (plus the version-bumped manifests and lesson/eval files from the prior round, already covered by adversarial-review-c.json/d.json, both 'continue').

Proof: read the prior gate-e.json (head 00c215b, parked) 'commands' check literal ruff output: exactly 3 I001 import-sort errors, in plugin/gate/checks.py:33, tests/test_gate.py:2441 and tests/test_lessons.py:8, each showing 'lessons' import needing to move before 'state'/'tests'. Grepped the repo for every 'from lessons import'/'import lessons' call site: exactly these three files, nothing missed. Read each file's current import block: checks.py now orders gate, gate.diff, gate.policy, hooks, hooks._common, lessons, state, state, state.status -- alphabetically correct, lessons after hooks._common and before state, matching the diff and resolving the literal reported error. Same check on test_gate.py and test_lessons.py: both now correctly ordered with lessons before state/tests, no blank line where the I001 error flagged one. The pyproject.toml diff adds exactly 'lessons' to known-first-party, consistent with isort's rule-of-cause stated in the comment.

Proof (formatting half): the comment also named 'ruff format --check . fails on tests/test_hooks.py (a blank line after `from hooks import shell_guard` in 46 tests)'. Grepped the current file: 'from hooks import shell_guard' occurs exactly 46 times, and every occurrence is followed by a blank line (spot-checked 20, counted all 46). This is an exact match to the comment's own number, not a rounded or claimed figure -- strong evidence the fix is what it claims to be and nothing more.

Blast radius (this round only): the five touched files are a lint/format-only diff (import order, one TOML list entry, blank lines); none of shell_guard.py's logic, hooks.json's wiring, or the sandbox settings changed in this round. No new behavior, no new caller, no migration, no guardrail file touched (guardrails check already verified 'ok' on the prior gate run and nothing in this round's diff is under .claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md or sdlc.yaml).

Policies: REVIEW.md's 'Do not report' section explicitly excludes 'anything CI already enforces (formatting, import order, lint rules that run in the hooks)' from review findings -- consistent with this being a mechanical, owner-directed lint fix rather than a design change requiring fresh policy scrutiny. coding-standards/security-baseline were already judged against the substantive design in adversarial-review-c.json and -d.json (both continue); this round changes no logic those policies would re-examine.

The tests: no test was added, removed or weakened by this round; it is exactly the kind of change (lint/format only) the project's own conventions treat as distinct from behavior. Did not re-run or cite gate/cli.py check, checks.py, any skill's check.py, or any claude-*.json/run-*.json/gate-*.json record as proof; relied only on the committed source files, the prior gate-e.json's literal ruff output (the deterministic toolchain's own recorded text, read for what the bug was, not as this round's verdict), and direct greps of the current tree.
